audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4]-whys[6] are shifted one row out of phase with their labels ('At 5' on the Level 6 row, 'Your level 6' on the First item row) and whys[6] declares the late game 'even/skill' while win[6] is Dr. Mundo.
audit.why: Dr. Mundo wins 57.22% over 1267 games and the full-layer phases already give him every stage from Level 3 on; the why text must state the same verdict as its own side field.
audit.corrected: whys realigned: Level 6 Dr. Mundo (Maximum Dosage), First item Dr. Mundo (HP stack), 2+ items Dr. Mundo (regen refills what Feast bites).

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes are described without the cooldowns that make them actionable — Rupture 6s, Feral Scream 11/10.5/10/9.5/9, Feast 80/70/60, Maximum Dosage 120s, Infected Bonesaw 4s.
audit.why: The advice 'all-in when Rupture is down' only becomes usable with the number attached, and the level-6 spike is decided by whether his ult is back before yours.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns written into spikes[0] and spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] credits 'Q healing' — Infected Bonesaw does no healing at all; and nothing on the page states that Dr. Mundo's passive resists the first immobilizing effect, i.e. the Rupture knockup.
audit.why: Riot's text: Q deals current-health damage and slows; W (Heart Zapper) is the heal; the passive resists the first Immobilizing effect and drops a canister that heals on pickup and lowers the passive's cooldown. Against a champion whose whole combo starts with a knockup this is the decisive interaction, and the mirror audit states it from Cho'Gath's side.
audit.corrected: Sustain attributed to passive regen and Heart Zapper; the passive eating the first Rupture knockup written into spikes[0]; Feral Scream named as the silence that shuts off Q and R.

edits.before: You out-sustain and out-trade Cho'Gath at level 1 with Q healing before his passive stacks.
edits.after: Passive regen and Heart Zapper out-last his level 1 before Carnivore starts feeding him.

edits.before: At 5 it stays even — his combo threatens but your health lets you survive it.
edits.after: At 6 Maximum Dosage out-heals the Rupture-Scream-Feast chain — Dr. Mundo.

edits.before: Your level 6 R heal and move speed shrug off his full Rupture-Scream-Feast combo.
edits.after: First item's HP stack beats his Vorpal Spikes chip outright — Dr. Mundo.

edits.before: Late, Feast true damage counters your health-stacking, evening the matchup to skill.
edits.after: Feast's true damage bites your HP stack, but your regen refills it — Dr. Mundo.

edits.before: With Q Infected Bonesaw sustaining you and E Blunt Force Trauma turning your missing health into raw damage, you out-trade Cho'Gath before he stacks his passive. Bait his Q Rupture by moving unpredictably; once it's on cooldown he has no reliable follow-up on your health bar.
edits.after: With Infected Bonesaw (Q) chunking his current health every 4s and Blunt Force (E) turning your missing health into damage, you out-trade Cho'Gath before Carnivore feeds him. Your passive eats the first Rupture knockup and drops a canister — walk it over to heal, then fight the 6s cooldown.

edits.before: Your R Maximum Dosage heal shrugs off a full Cho'Gath combo. He needs to land Rupture into Scream (W silence) into Feast, and even his true-damage ult rarely one-shots a Mundo who ults for the burst of health and move speed.
edits.after: Maximum Dosage (R) heals a percent of your missing health, so his full combo only feeds it. He must chain Rupture into Feral Scream — an 11s-cooldown silence that shuts off your Q and R — into Feast; break any link and the fight is yours.

edits.before: Dodge his Rupture so his combo whiffs
edits.after: Bait Rupture on your passive, then fight
